facts: M/I Homes delivered 8,921 homes in 2025 with revenue of $4.4 billion, while pretax income (excluding $59 million in inventory and warranty charges) was nearly $590 million, down 20% from last year's record $734 million.
Fourth quarter new contracts increased 9% year-over-year, with October up 18%, November up 6%, and December up 4%.
Full year gross margins excluding charges were 24.4%, down 220 basis points from 2024 due to higher incentives and lot costs.
The company ended 2025 with $689 million in cash, zero borrowings under its $900 million credit facility, resulting in a debt-to-capital ratio of 18% and net debt-to-cap ratio of 0.
Shareholders' equity increased 8% year-over-year to a record $3.2 billion, with book value per share reaching $123.
The financial services segment achieved a record capture rate of 93% for the full year with pretax income of $56 million.

Fourth quarter inventory charges totaled $40 million (including $30 million of impairments primarily in entry-level communities with ASPs below $375,000) plus $11 million in warranty charges from two Florida communities.
The company spent $200 million on share repurchases in 2025 and has repurchased 13% of outstanding shares over the last three years.
Construction costs decreased approximately 2% in 2025 while cycle time improved by about 5%.
Approximately 79% of fourth quarter sales were inventory (spec) homes compared to 67% a year ago, with the company now running 65-75% of sales from specs on an ongoing basis.
Q3 2025 net sales were $114.6 million, down 3.8% year-over-year but exceeding company expectations.
Q3 adjusted EBITDA was $30.8 million with a 26.9% margin, compared to 37.5% margin in Q3 2024.
Professional channel net sales grew 5.3% year-over-year in Q3 to $44.5 million, while specialty retail declined 13.5% to $36.9 million and DTC declined 2.9% to $33.3 million.
Year-to-date adjusted gross profit margin is 72.2%, flat year-over-year, while Q3 adjusted gross profit margin of 71.5% was up 70 basis points year-over-year.
Sales and marketing investment increased $6.2 million year-over-year in Q3 and approximately $20.8 million year-to-date.
The company ended Q3 with cash and cash equivalents of $286.4 million and debt of $352.1 million.
Inventory was $73.3 million at quarter end, down approximately $12.6 million from the prior year's $85.9 million.
Year-to-date U.S. net sales were down approximately 4%, while international sales were up approximately 2%.
The Blitz program drove sell-through that was on average at least mid-teens percentage higher in the 2 months following events versus the 2 months prior in targeted cities.
Full year 2025 guidance was maintained with net sales expected in the range of -3% to +2% versus fiscal year 2024 and adjusted EBITDA margin of 20% to 22%.
Full year 2025 EPS was $3.14, representing a 73% year-over-year increase, and adjusted return on equity was 24.4%, up 67% from the prior year.
Trinity introduced 2026 EPS guidance of $1.85 to $2.10, with expected industry deliveries of approximately 25,000 railcars, well below replacement levels.
The Napier Park railcar partnership restructuring resulted in a $194 million noncash gain in Q4 2025, with the transacted Triumph fleet value significantly exceeding book value.

Trinity estimates the market value of its 101,000 wholly owned railcars (carried at $6.3 billion cost) is approximately 35% to 45% higher than carrying value, reflecting roughly 3% to 4% annual asset appreciation over 20 years.
Rail Products delivered a full year operating margin of 5.2% despite deliveries declining 46% year-over-year, and the company expects 5% to 6% margins in 2026.

In 2025, approximately 31,000 railcars were delivered industry-wide while more than 38,000 were retired, resulting in net fleet contraction, with railcars in storage rising above 21% for the first time since 2021.

Trinity expects secondary market gains of $120 million to $140 million in 2026, including anticipated gains from contributing remaining partially owned railcars to the managed Napier Park fleet in Q2.

Full year 2025 cash flow from continuing operations was $367 million, and Trinity returned $170 million to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases, with 7 consecutive years of dividend growth at a 9% annualized rate.

Net lease fleet investment guidance for 2026 is $450 million to $550 million, up from $350 million in 2025, and the company expects to reach the top end of its 3-year $750 million to $1 billion investment target.

Fleet utilization remained strong at 97.1% with renewal lease rates 27% higher than expiring rates in Q4, and the Future Lease Rate Differential remained positive for the 18th consecutive quarter at 6%.
Core Natural Resources reported Q3 2025 net income of $32 million ($0.61 per diluted share) and adjusted EBITDA of $141 million.
The company generated $39 million of free cash flow in Q3 2025 ($88 million operating cash flow minus $49 million capital expenditures) despite weak commodity prices.
Year-to-date, Core has returned $218 million to shareholders, representing approximately 100% of free cash flow generation, including $19 million in Q3 share repurchases and $5 million in dividends.
Total liquidity at the end of Q3 2025 was $995 million, an increase of $47 million compared to the end of Q2.

The company secured 26 million tons of forward contracts, increasing its 2026 High CV Thermal book by 4 million tons to nearly 17 million tons and its PRB book by 8 million tons to more than 40 million tons.

The metallurgical segment's coking coal sales volume guidance was lowered to 7.4-7.8 million tons due to timing delays in the Leer South longwall restart caused by MSHA personnel unavailability during a government shutdown.

Year-to-date Leer South fire and idling costs total approximately $75 million, with an additional $15-$25 million expected in Q4, while the company received $19 million in insurance recovery advances.
Capital expenditure guidance was lowered by $40 million to a range of $260-$290 million due to attractive equipment financing obtained throughout the year.
U.S. coal-fired generation has increased approximately 12% year-to-date, with the PJM RTO market up approximately 16%, driven by robust power demand.
U.S. data center power demand is expected to nearly triple by 2030, rising from approximately 76 gigawatts in 2026 to 134 gigawatts in 2030.

Abeona had cash, cash equivalents, restricted cash and short-term investments totaling $207.5 million as of September 30, 2025, expected to fund operations for over 2 years without accounting for ZEVASKYN revenue.
First patient treatment for ZEVASKYN has been delayed to Q4 2025 due to a false positive result from a rapid sterility release assay that was an FDA requirement added during the BLA review.

The number of identified eligible patients at qualified treatment centers who are motivated to initiate treatment has more than doubled to approximately 30 patients, up from 12-plus mentioned on the Q2 call.
Abeona has received ZEVASKYN product order forms (ZPOFs) for 12 patients, with insurance prior authorizations already obtained for several of them.

Policies covering ZEVASKYN have been published by all major commercial payers including UnitedHealthcare, Cigna, Aetna, Anthem and the majority of Blue Cross Blue Shield plans, collectively covering more than 80% of all commercially insured lives.
ZEVASKYN received baseline coverage across all 51 state Medicaid programs and Puerto Rico effective October 1, 2025.
CMS has established a permanent product J-code for ZEVASKYN that will go into effect on January 1, 2026.
Net loss was $5.2 million for Q3 2025 (negative $0.10 per share) compared to a net loss of $30.3 million in Q3 2024 (negative $0.63 per share).
The company expects to achieve profitability in the first half of 2026, with the delay in first patient treatment not significantly impacting that timeline.
A manufacturing shutdown for routine FDA-mandated maintenance is scheduled from mid-December to early January.
Applied Materials expects to grow its semiconductor equipment business more than 20% in calendar year 2026, with demand weighted towards the second half of the year.
Q1 fiscal 2026 revenue was $7 billion, at the upper end of guidance, with non-GAAP EPS of $2.38 at the top of the guidance range.
Q2 guidance calls for revenue of $7.65 billion (plus or minus $500 million), up approximately 9% sequentially, with non-GAAP EPS of $2.64 (plus or minus $0.20).
Revenue from China declined 7% year-over-year and represented 27% of combined semi equipment and AGS sales and 30% of overall sales.
Applied Global Services delivered record revenue of $1.56 billion, growing 15% year-over-year, with non-GAAP operating margin expanding 320 basis points.
Cold field emission eBeam technology revenues are expected to double in calendar 2026 to more than $1 billion, making process diagnostics and control one of Applied's fastest-growing businesses.
Non-GAAP gross margin for the Semiconductor Systems segment increased 100 basis points year-over-year to more than 54%, driven by value-based pricing and manufacturing cost improvements.
Applied has proactively increased inventory by nearly $500 million year-over-year and has nearly doubled its system manufacturing capacity over the past several years to meet rising demand.
An accrual of $252.5 million was recorded related to an export controls compliance matter, with the DOJ and SEC closing their inquiries with no enforcement actions.
ICAPS and China wafer fab equipment spending are expected to be approximately flat year-over-year in 2026, while NAND is expected to remain less than 10% of total wafer fab equipment spending.
Q4 2025 revenue was $994.2 million, a 2.6% organic decline year-over-year, while full year 2025 revenue was $4.02 billion with an organic revenue decrease of 1.6%.
The DSA net book-to-bill improved to 1.12x in Q4 2025 on net bookings of $665 million, up from 0.82x in Q3, with the DSA backlog rising to $1.86 billion from $1.80 billion at the end of Q3.
Biotech funding reached a record $28 billion in Q4 2025, and biotech clients were the primary driver behind sequentially improving DSA net book-to-bill in each month of the second half of 2025.

2026 guidance calls for organic revenue ranging from down 1% to at least flat, operating margin improvement of 20 to 50 basis points from 19.8%, and non-GAAP EPS of $10.70 to $11.20 (approximately 4% to 9% growth).

The K.F. (Cambodia) acquisition is expected to add approximately $0.25 to EPS in 2026 and approximately $0.60 in accretion by 2027, with more than 50 basis points of consolidated operating margin improvement and more than 100 basis points in the DSA segment in 2026.

Q1 2026 non-GAAP EPS is expected to decline at a high-teens rate year-over-year, with an operating margin in the mid-teens due to NHP shipment timing, ~$0.15 EPS headwind from accelerated stock compensation related to the CEO transition, and higher DSA sourcing costs.

The company expects to generate at least $100 million in incremental cost savings above 2025 levels, bringing cumulative annualized cost savings from actions over the last three years to over $300 million.

Free cash flow for 2026 is expected to be $375 million to $400 million, down from $518.5 million in 2025, primarily due to higher bonus payments and deferred compensation related to the CEO retirement.

The 2026 non-GAAP tax rate is expected to decrease to 22%-23% from 24.6% in 2025, driven by the One Big Beautiful Bill Act and favorable geographic mix, contributing more than $0.30 per share in below-the-line EPS benefit at guidance midpoint.
Planned divestitures totaling approximately 7% of 2025 annual revenue are expected to close by mid-2026, with annualized non-GAAP EPS accretion of $0.30 but closer to $0.10 for the partial year 2026.

Q1 2026 revenue was $1 billion with adjusted EBITDA of $126 million, reflecting record pumping efficiencies and high fleet utilization while absorbing full pricing headwinds and winter weather disruption.

Q1 net income was $23 million ($0.14 diluted EPS) versus $14 million prior quarter, while adjusted net income was $10 million ($0.06 adjusted diluted EPS), excluding $12 million of tax-effected gains on investments.
Liberty executed $1.3 billion in convertible debt offerings during Q1 at a 0% coupon with capped calls at a 150% premium, resulting in a net cost of capital below 3% to fund power growth.
The company ended Q1 with $699 million cash, $579 million net debt (up $360 million from converts), and total liquidity of $1.2 billion.

Management expects Q2 revenue to grow high single digits sequentially with normal incremental margins, driven mostly by activity with a small amount of pricing recovery, while meaningful pricing impact is expected in Q3.
Liberty plans approximately $300 million in contract milestone payments in Q2 or early Q3 to secure generation capacity supporting its 3 gigawatt deployed power goal by 2029.
2026 CapEx guidance is unchanged at approximately $1 billion (with ~$250 million on the completions side), with potential upside if a digiFleet becomes incremental rather than replacement capacity.

Over 70% of Liberty's digiPrime fleet will gain variable speed capabilities and increased horsepower via a software upgrade, enabling a path to 100% natural gas operations and potential fuel savings of north of $20 million annualized per fleet versus 100% diesel.

Liberty has committed 400 megawatts to Vantage starting in early 2027 under a development partnership with payments mirroring an ESA equivalent over a 5-year period for the generation portion (~55-60% of plant capex).

A previously announced 330-megawatt data center expansion was canceled by the hyperscaler, but the developer paid a multimillion dollar cancellation fee and those megawatts have been reallocated to a different opportunity in the same time frame.

Third quarter total product revenue increased approximately 13% over the prior quarter to about $68 million, including Amtagvi sales of approximately $58 million and global Proleukin revenue of nearly $10 million.
Gross margin improved to approximately 43% in Q3, with cost of sales reduced by approximately 21% over the prior quarter.
The company reiterated its full year 2025 revenue guidance range of $250 million to $300 million.
Cash position was approximately $307 million as of September 30, expected to fund operations into the second quarter of 2027.
Total costs and expenses were reduced by approximately 10% over the prior quarter, excluding restructuring charges of approximately $5 million.
Interim LUN-202 lung cancer trial data showed an objective response rate of 26% with median duration of response not reached at more than 25 months of follow-up.

The non-small cell lung cancer market opportunity is approximately 7x larger than the melanoma opportunity, with potential U.S. peak sales of $10 billion and approximately 50,000 addressable patients in the U.S. alone.
Amtagvi peak sales are projected at more than $1 billion in the U.S. for melanoma alone.
Costs associated with patient drop-off and manufacturing out-specs have decreased by 40% since the beginning of the year to approximately $9 million this quarter.
All Amtagvi and clinical manufacturing will transition to the internal facility (iCTC) in early 2026, eliminating the need for a contract manufacturer and expected to further improve gross margins.
Total revenue for 2025 grew 10% to $27 billion with underlying revenue growth of 4%, while adjusted operating income increased 11% to $7.3 billion.
The company achieved its 18th consecutive year of reported margin expansion with adjusted operating margin improving 30 basis points.
Free cash flow grew 25% to $5 billion in 2025, up from $4 billion in 2024.
The company returned record capital to shareholders with $2 billion in share repurchases (the largest annual amount in company history) and a 10% increase in the quarterly dividend.
Global property insurance rates decreased 9% year-over-year in Q4, while U.S. excess casualty rates increased 19%, reflecting ongoing pressure in the liability environment.
The Thrive program is expected to generate $400 million of total savings and incur approximately $500 million of charges over the next 3 years.
Management expects underlying revenue growth in 2026 to be similar to 2025, with continued margin expansion and solid adjusted EPS growth.
The company plans to deploy approximately $5 billion of capital in 2026 across dividends, acquisitions, and share repurchases.
Assets under management at Mercer reached $692 billion at quarter end, up 12% compared to Q4 of the prior year.

Management estimates approximately $3 trillion in digital infrastructure investment over the next 5 years, with 2,000 to 3,000 data centers expected to be constructed worldwide, representing a significant growth opportunity for the company.

Q1 2026 revenues of $983.3 million increased 9.5% year-over-year (6.8% excluding FX), driven by growth in Corporate Finance, Strategic Communications, and Technology, partially offset by a decline in Economic Consulting.
Net income decreased to $57.6 million from $61.8 million, and adjusted EBITDA fell to $96.8 million (9.8% margin) from $115.2 million (12.8% margin) in the prior year quarter.
EPS was $1.90 versus $1.74 prior year; the prior year included a $0.55 special charge, so adjusted EPS comparison is $1.90 vs. $2.29.
The company maintained its 2026 full-year guidance of $3.94B–$4.10B revenue and $8.90–$9.60 EPS, with full-year tax rate expected at 22%–24% despite Q1's elevated 26.6% rate.

Corporate Finance revenues grew 19.2% to $409.5 million with turnaround/restructuring up 19%, transactions up 18%, and transformation up 20%; segment adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 21.6% from 16.3%.
Strategic Communications delivered record revenues of $103 million (up 18.4%) and record adjusted segment EBITDA of $21.9 million with margin expanding to 21.3% from 14.8%.

Economic Consulting (Compass Lexecon) revenues declined 2.3% to $175.6 million and posted an adjusted segment EBITDA loss of $5.9 million versus $14.4 million profit prior year, with management calling Q1 the EBITDA low point but warning of multiple quarters of rebuild ahead.
FLC underperformed expectations with revenues up only 1.2% to $192.9 million and adjusted segment EBITDA margin contracting to 13.1% from 19.7% due to higher compensation, hiring costs, and bad debt.

Total debt net of cash rose to $556.7 million from $99.9 million at year-end 2025, driven by annual bonus payments and share repurchases of 787,098 shares at an average $161.11 (total $126.8 million), with $354.9 million remaining under the buyback authorization.

Management expects 2026 SG&A to be approximately $60 million higher than 2025, with Q2 2026 as the peak (~$5 million above Q1), and announced 29 SMD/affiliate hires year-to-date on top of 85 senior hires in 2025, with plans to accelerate junior hiring in H2.
Everus delivered fourth quarter 2025 revenues exceeding $1 billion for the first time in its history, up 33% from the prior year period.
Full year 2025 EBITDA was $319.8 million, up 52% compared to 2024 after adjusting for incremental stand-alone operating costs of $28 million annualized.
Total backlog at December 31, 2025 was $3.23 billion, up 16% year-over-year, with T&D backlog up 41% and E&M backlog up 13%.
The company is guiding 2026 revenues of $4.1 billion to $4.2 billion and EBITDA of $320 million to $335 million, implying approximately 11% revenue growth and 2% EBITDA growth at midpoints.
Net leverage stood at approximately 0.4x net debt to trailing 12-month EBITDA as of December 31, 2025, well below the stated long-term target of 1.5x to 2.0x.
Full year 2025 revenues increased 31.5% to $3.75 billion, driven by 44% growth in E&M segment revenues.
E&M segment fourth quarter EBITDA increased 57% year-over-year to $67.1 million, with segment EBITDA margin expanding 70 basis points to 8.5%.
The company ended 2025 with approximately 9,400 employees, an 8.5% increase from 8,700 at the end of 2024.
Approximately 80% of backlog historically burns off within 12 months, providing clear revenue visibility for 2026 and some momentum into 2027.
Free cash flow for 2025 was $100 million, down from $128.8 million in 2024, reflecting increased working capital investment and CapEx of $66.8 million versus $43.8 million in 2024.
CACI delivered Q1 FY2026 revenue of nearly $2.3 billion, representing 11.2% year-over-year growth with 5.5% organic growth.
Q1 free cash flow was $143 million with EBITDA margin of 11.7%, a 120 basis point year-over-year improvement.
The company won $5 billion in contract awards in Q1, representing a book-to-bill of 2.2x for the quarter and 1.3x on a trailing 12-month basis.
Adjusted diluted earnings per share of $6.85 were 16% higher than the prior year period.
Record backlog reached $34 billion, up 4% year-over-year, while funded backlog grew nearly 26% year-over-year.
Management reaffirmed FY2026 guidance for revenue of $9.2-$9.4 billion, EBITDA margin in the mid-11% range, adjusted net income of $605-$625 million, and free cash flow of at least $710 million.
Over 92% of FY2026 revenue is now expected from existing programs, with less than 4% from recompetes and 4% from new business.
The company has $6 billion of bids under evaluation with approximately 80% for new business, and expects to submit another $13 billion in bids over the next two quarters.
CACI's portfolio of electronic warfare technologies, including Counter-UAS, generates approximately $2 billion of revenue annually.
The weighted average duration of Q1 contract awards was over 6 years, and the company expanded international sales to 15 NATO countries.

Cytokinetics ended Q3 2025 with approximately $1.25 billion in cash and investments, and expects to finish 2025 with approximately $1.2 billion after receiving $100 million from Royalty Pharma's Tranche 5 loan in October.

The company raised net proceeds of $327 million from the issuance of $750 million aggregate principal amount of convertible senior notes due 2031 and concurrent exchange of $399.5 million of 2027 notes.
Net loss for Q3 2025 was $306.2 million ($2.55 per share), including a $121.2 million debt conversion expense, compared to a net loss of $160.5 million ($1.36 per share) in Q3 2024.
Full year 2025 GAAP operating expense guidance was narrowed to $680 million to $700 million, with stock-based compensation expected between $110 million and $120 million.

The company expects potential FDA approval of aficamten for oHCM by the PDUFA date at the end of 2025, with full commercial launch inclusive of product availability and REMS operations to follow in early January.
Top line results from the primary cohort of ACACIA-HCM (Phase 3 trial in nonobstructive HCM) are expected in the second quarter of 2026.
The company expects a final decision from the European Commission on aficamten approval in the first half of 2026, with a Germany launch planned for the first half of 2026.
Current CMI penetration is approximately 15% to 20% of the oHCM market, with management expecting penetration to increase around 5 percentage points each year.

The commercial sales team averages over 20 years of industry experience and 14 years of cardiovascular experience, with a goal to reach nearly all of the estimated 650 HCPs representing approximately 80% of HCM prescribing within the first few weeks of January.
Over 75% of COMET-HF trial sites in North America and Europe are now activated, with patient enrollment expected to continue into 2026.
Ball Corporation delivered record comparable diluted EPS of $3.57 in 2025, a 13% increase from 2024.
Adjusted free cash flow reached a record $956 million in 2025, up 2.4x year-over-year.
The company returned $1.54 billion to shareholders in 2025 through combined share repurchases and dividends.
Fourth quarter 2025 global shipped volumes increased 6%, with full year growth of 4.1%, exceeding the company's long-term volume growth range.
EMEA segment comparable operating earnings increased 36.7% in Q4 and 19% for full year 2025, with profit per can reaching an all-time record.
The company expects approximately $35 million in combined costs in 2026 from Millersburg plant start-up and tariff-related ends production domestication in North America.

Ball closed the acquisition of two Benepack beverage can facilities in Belgium and Hungary, expected to contribute approximately 1.7 billion units of volume in 2026 with comparable operating earnings close to flat.
Since 2019, EMEA and North American businesses have expanded profit per can by more than 30%.
Management expects 2026 comparable diluted EPS growth of 10% or more, with free cash flow greater than $900 million.
Share count was reduced to 265 million shares, representing a 16% reduction over the past two years, with at least $600 million in additional repurchases planned for 2026.
Oklo ended Q3 2025 with approximately $1.2 billion in cash and marketable securities on its balance sheet.
Oklo's Q3 2025 operating loss was $36.3 million, including $9.1 million in noncash stock-based compensation expense.
Oklo completed an at-the-market fundraising program in Q3 generating $540 million in gross proceeds.
The company expects full-year 2025 cash used in operating activities to be within the guided range of $65 million to $80 million.
Oklo received 3 of the 11 awards under the Department of Energy's Reactor Pilot Program.
The company announced its Advanced Fuel Center in Tennessee representing an investment of up to $1.68 billion and creating more than 800 permanent jobs.
The government announced up to 20 tons of plutonium being made available as bridge fuel, which could be converted into approximately 180 metric tons of Aurora fuel.
Oklo's customer pipeline remains at 14 gigawatts, predominantly comprised of data center and hyperscaler customers.
The Atomic Alchemy pilot facility is targeting to be operational by mid-2026.
Oklo's partnership with newcleo could bring up to $2 billion in investment through an affiliated vehicle to expand U.S. fuel fabrication capacity.
Q1 2026 total sales were up 5% year-over-year, with the Core Collectibles business up 17%.
Funko reported its highest-ever gross margin of 44% in Q1, driving adjusted EBITDA of $11 million, well above expectations.
Q2 2026 guidance calls for sales growth of low-to-mid single digits and adjusted EBITDA between $5 million and $10 million.
Full-year 2026 guidance was reiterated at sales flat to up 3% and adjusted EBITDA of $70 million to $80 million, with current tariff rates running slightly below plan.
Global POS was up 6% in Q1, with wholesale POS up 12%, U.S. up 6%, and Europe up 28%, indicating healthy sell-in/sell-through alignment.

Loungefly is undergoing a planned reset with SKUs cut by 50%, leading to expected sales declines this year but improved SKU productivity and profitability, while bag charms and pins are driving double-digit growth.
Funko has paid approximately $20 million in IEEPA tariffs and is pursuing refunds plus exploring monetization of tariff claims, representing potential upside.
Full-year gross margin guidance is 42%–44%, supported by reduced discounting/promotions, renewed licensing agreements with major partners, and favorable channel/sales mix.
Loungefly's first Swarovski collection sold out within hours at a $400 price point, well above the typical $80–$90 average, with more premium launches planned.

Management is investing in international expansion under new Chief International Officer Andy Oddie, citing opportunities in Latin America and Asia (e.g., Zootopia grossed ~$630M in China), and hired former Nike executive Nik Rupp as Head of Marketing and Brand.
Q1 2026 revenue grew 10.8% year-over-year, and American expects Q2 revenue growth of approximately 15% (guidance range of 13.5% to 16.5%), with 65% of Q2 already booked.

Q1 included a $320 million revenue impact from winter storms and a $400 million increase in fuel expense versus the January forward curve, resulting in an adjusted loss per diluted share of $0.40, though pretax margin still improved ~2 points year-over-year.

Full-year 2026 guidance midpoint is $0.35 EPS (approximately flat to 2025) despite jet fuel prices increasing fuel expense by over $4 billion year-over-year, with Q2 EPS guided to a range of -$0.20 to +$0.20 assuming ~$4/gallon fuel.
Management expects to recapture roughly 40%-50% of higher fuel costs in Q2, 75%-85% in Q3, and into the 90s in Q4 (assuming industry capacity reductions if fuel remains elevated).

Q2 capacity was cut about 1 point below initial plans (from ~6% growth) via suspended Tel Aviv and Doha flying, Chicago reductions, and marginal domestic cuts, with further off-peak capacity cuts possible for August/September.

Q1 domestic PRASM rose 6.6%, Atlantic unit revenue jumped 16.7% (London +25%), Pacific unit revenue increased 7.8%, and Latin America was slightly negative due to Mexico; Q2 domestic unit revenue is expected to grow more than 10%.
Managed corporate revenue increased 13% year-over-year and small/medium enterprise managed business product was up 28%, with banking, healthcare/pharma, and industrials leading verticals.

Premium unit revenue outpaced Main Cabin by 7 points year-over-year, with paid load factors in business and premium economy at record highs (~10 points above 2019); co-brand card spend rose 9% and AAdvantage enrollments jumped 25% year-over-year.

Q1 CASMx rose 5.2% (pressured ~2 points by storm-related capacity loss) and Q2 CASMx is guided up 2%-4%; the company expects over $200 million of incremental savings in 2026, bringing cumulative reengineering savings to ~$1 billion.

American ended Q1 with nearly $11 billion in liquidity and reduced total debt by $1.8 billion to $34.7 billion (first time below $35 billion since mid-2015); 2026 aircraft deliveries were cut from 55 to 49, lowering CapEx by ~$300 million to approximately $4 billion.
PPL achieved 2025 ongoing earnings of $1.81 per share, representing 7.1% growth from prior year results and in line with the midpoint of guidance.
PPL issued 2026 ongoing earnings guidance of $1.90 to $1.98 per share, with a midpoint of $1.94 per share representing 7.2% growth from 2025.
The company's updated capital investment plan projects $23 billion from 2026 through 2029, up $3 billion from the prior plan, supporting an estimated rate base CAGR of approximately 10.3%.
PPL expects total equity needs of about $3 billion from 2026 to 2029, of which approximately $1 billion was already executed in 2025, leaving about $2 billion to be issued going forward.

The Kentucky Public Service Commission approved an aggregate increase of approximately $233 million in annual electric and gas revenues with allowed ROEs of 9.775%, which are 35 basis points higher than previously approved levels.

Data center projects in advanced stages in PPL Electric's Pennsylvania service territory now total approximately 25.2 gigawatts, up 23% since the last quarterly update, with at least 10 gigawatts expected to be under ESAs by end of Q1 2026.

PPL outperformed its O&M savings target by about $20 million, achieving approximately $170 million in run rate savings from the 2021 baseline, about a year ahead of the $175 million target set for end of 2026.

The company modified its annual dividend growth rate target to 4% to 6% while issuing equity and declared a quarterly dividend of $0.285 per share, representing a nearly 5% increase from the prior quarterly dividend.

PPL's Kentucky pipeline reflects more than 9 gigawatts of potential new load through the early 2030s, with probability-weighted demand growth projections of about 2.8 gigawatts, roughly 1 gigawatt more than reflected in the 2025 CPCN load forecast.

The Blackstone joint venture has no earnings contributions or CapEx embedded in the updated business plan, but depending on timing of hyperscaler agreements and generation mix, earnings contributions could come as early as the back end of the 2026-2029 planning horizon.
Full year 2025 net revenues were $175.1 million, representing 217% year-over-year growth, with Q4 revenue of $57.6 million at the high end of the $170 million to $175 million guided range.

Q4 cash operating expenses were $50.3 million, better than the less than $55 million target, and full year cash operating expenses of approximately $284 million came in at the low end of guidance, reflecting nearly 50% quarterly reduction over the last three quarters of 2025.

The company issued 2026 net revenue guidance of $320 million to $345 million, which includes an approximately $17 million to $20 million favorable impact from an accounting reclassification of certain third-party charges from gross-to-net adjustments to cost of goods sold.

The term loan was modified to extend maturity from December 2027 to February 2029, reduce interest rate from 12% to 9.85%, and reduce outstanding principal to $175 million after using approximately $56 million in cash.

Following a $130 million gross proceeds equity offering in January and the term debt modification, the company has approximately $190 million in cash and believes this plus anticipated future operating cash flow will be sufficient to satisfy all debt obligations and covenants.
The company anticipates achieving operational profitability (excluding stock-based compensation) by Q3 2026 and for full year 2026, with cash flow positivity expected in 2027.
